scopes.description:
Scopes are what it may do (D398); absent, for a token made before scopes, it has
every scope its user's role allows.

takingTasks.description:
TakingTasks says the token waits for the tasks of your Local agent nodes now, or did
a moment ago (D413).

token.description: Token is the secret, present only in the response that creates it.

held.description: Held is what of the paper cash resting buys hold back.

open.description:
Open is false until the workflow's first paper order; the rest is then what an
account would start with.

resetAt.description: ResetAt is when it was last started over: orders before it are history.

wallet.description: Live: the wallet trading, and whether its pUSD, the cash, could be read.

worth.description:
Worth is the cash and what the holdings are worth now. Profit is, on paper, the
worth less what the account started with; live, what the holdings made, sold and
still held.

confirmed.description: Confirmed says you confirmed it first, as it waited for you (D406).

how.description:
How: it ran this by hand (run), switched its workflow on (switched_on), or changed it
while on (changed).

id.description: ID is the agent's grant, or the token: the orders' filter takes kind:id.

answer.description: Answer lets them answer the questions the user's workflows ask (D405).

delete.description:
Delete lets them delete workflows, custom nodes and credentials; Share, share
workflows to the library (D403, D404).

seePersonal.description:
SeePersonal lets agents and API tokens see the workflows' personal settings, such as
webhook URLs.

useCredentials.description:
UseCredentials lets them save and run workflows that use credentials, test
credentials and change where they go (D404).

beforeRestart.description:
BeforeRestart says it was open as the server restarted, and its agent has not come
back since; it opens a new one when it calls again.

client.description: Client is its client as it said, with its version, like claude-code 2.1.300.

kind.description: Kind is agent, signed in with OAuth, or token, an API token.

name.description: Name is the agent's or the token's, as it was when the session opened.

address.description: Address is where agents connect, such as https://polythought.example.com/mcp.

clients.description: Clients are those the steps are for, a tab each, in order.

enabled.description: Enabled says agents may connect here; off, an admin turned Agents over MCP off.

metadata.description: Metadata is where an agent finds how to sign in (RFC 9728).

caps.description:
Caps are those that apply, 0 for none; Own, an admin's for the user, those left out
being the instance's.

inputTokens.description:
Tokens are every call's; dollars, what providers reported, which only some do
(OpenRouter): CostedCalls of Calls.

killStopsAgents.description: KillStopsAgents is the user's choice that their kill switch stops their agents too.

version.description: Version is the newest release, which the check found.

name.description: Name is what it is for people, like "pUSD to the CTF Exchange".

granting.description: Granting is how many approvals it grants; none when none were missing.

kind.description: Kind is the wallet's: 1 a proxy wallet, 2 a Safe, 3 a Deposit Wallet.

owner.description: Owner signed, or signs, for the wallet.

state.description:
State: signing waits for the owner's signature, submitted for the chain; a failed one
says why in error.

message.description: Message is what a Safe's owner signs, hex, with personal_sign.

typedData.description: TypedData is what a Deposit Wallet's owner signs, with eth_signTypedData_v4.

missing.description: Missing are those Polymarket's index shows missing, which may be a minute behind.

ready.description: Ready says no trading approval is missing (D160).

setup.description: Setup is the last setting up of them here.

way.description:
Way is how they can be set up here: with the imported key, in the owner's browser
wallet, or not at all (no Builder key; an EOA, or a proxy wallet without a key).

why.description: Why says why not, when Way is none.

permissions.description:
Permissions are those the version asks for, which the admin approves: exactly
those, or the approval is refused.

minPasswordLength.description: MinPasswordLength is the fewest characters a new password may have.

passwordReset.description: PasswordReset says a forgotten password can be reset by email (D176).

requests.description: Requests says people without an invite can ask for one (D394).

path.description: Path is the file's in the @polythought/sdk package, like index.d.ts.

inRunners.description: InRunners says code runs in runner processes; false, in the server's.

lastError.description:
LastError says why one last stopped; Failed why they would not start, every code
run failing (D358).

restarts.description: runners started again since the server started

running.description: of them, now: one that stopped starts with the next run

why.description: Why says why they are not sandboxed, when they are not.

files.description:
Files of @polythought/sdk, for an editor to load as that package: index.d.ts
exports the others.

token.description: Token is the one in the mailed link.

about.description: About is whom it is about, such as a user's email: yours to see, never the agent's.

asker.description: Asker is who asked: the agent by name, or "an API token".

decidedVia.description:
DecidedVia is where you decided it: in the app, on Telegram, or in the agent's own
window (D409).

detail.description:
Detail is what it changes, a line each, such as a workflow's nodes and settings
against the graph it has (A3).

result.description: Result is what came of it: an execution, or why it failed.

what.description: What says what it does, such as Run "Spread watch" by hand, which trades live.

code.description: Code is typed (D393): 8 to 64 letters, digits, - and _, any case; made when empty.

email.description:
Email, when given, mails the invite there, and only that address signs up with it,
once (D371): the server makes its code and it lasts Invite lifetime, so it takes no
code, uses or end.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is when it ends, within a year; Invite lifetime from now when absent.

maxUses.description: MaxUses is how many sign-ups it admits, 1 to 1000; 1 when absent.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt left out means the token never expires.

scopes.description: Scopes are what it may do (D398): at least one; admin for an admin's token only.

secrets.description: Secrets names the secret values that are set; the values themselves are never sent.

testedAt.description:
TestedAt is absent until the credential is tested. TestError says why the last test
failed, and is absent when it passed.

values.description: Values holds the values that are not secret, by field name.

secret.description: Secret values are write-only: stored encrypted and never sent back.

testable.description: Testable types can be tried against their service.

hasKey.description:
HasKey says they were made from a key, which is kept too: an imported private key,
or a session key (SessionKey).

name.description:
Name makes its type, custom.<name>: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting
with a letter, up to 40. It cannot change.

outputs.description: Outputs are its output ports, in order; it has one input, main.

source.description:
Source is TypeScript exporting run(items, ctx), which gets every item at once and
returns the items, or with several outputs, { port: items }.

type.description: Type is what workflows name it by: custom.<name>.

name.description:
Name makes its type, custom.<name>: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting
with a letter, up to 40. It cannot change.

outputs.description: Outputs are its output ports, in order; it has one input, main.

source.description:
Source is TypeScript exporting run(items, ctx), which gets every item at once and
returns the items, or with several outputs, { port: items }.

field.description:
Field marks a string, or each element of a list, as a path to a field of the items
the node receives; FieldKinds, when present, are the kinds that field may be.

name.description: Name is what code reads it as: ctx.params.<name>.

options.description: Options are the choices of a string, or of each element of a list.

hidden.description:
Hidden are the parts you hid, by the app's names for them, such as traders; the
rest show.

code.description: Code is stable and meant for programs, e.g. invalid_workflow or not_found.

problems.description:
Problems lists everything wrong with a submitted workflow (code invalid_workflow),
with changed settings (code invalid_input, param is the setting's key) or with a
credential (code invalid_input, param is "name" or "values.<field>"), with a
custom node (code invalid_input, param is the part of its form: "name",
"settings.0.default", "outputs.1", "items", "source"), or with workflow code that
does not compile (code invalid_code, with line and column).

workflows.description:
Workflows lists the workflows a change to a custom node would break (code
breaks_workflows), with what is wrong in each.

by.description: By is the agent or token behind it (D407): absent for you.

waitingOn.description:
WaitingOn is the node a waiting execution paused at, and WaitingUntil when the wait
ends at the latest.

nextCursor.description: NextCursor is absent on the last page.

call.description: Call is each, an answer for each item, or together, one for all of them.

heldBy.description:
HeldBy is the agent or token that has it, by its name, until heldUntil; absent while
it waits for one to take it.

prompt.description: Prompt is what it asks, together; each item has its own.

schema.description: Schema is the JSON schema an answer keeps to, answering in fields or to a schema.

until.description: Until is when the run stops waiting, and its items fail.

blocked.description:
Blocked says Polymarket refuses orders from the server's IP, or restricts only its
website there, which the answer does not tell apart.

checked.description:
Checked says Polymarket answered at least once; the fields below are its last
answer.

error.description: Error says why the last check failed, when it did; the answer before stays.

cost.description:
Cost is what the shares held cost, fees included; Realized is the profit or loss
of those sold.

Cost is what the shares held cost, fees included; Realized is the profit or loss
of those sold.

mark.description:
Mark is a share's price now, the book's midpoint; absent when nobody knows, and
Value is then the cost.

privateKey.description: PrivateKey is 64 hex digits, with 0x or without.

newPermissions.description:
NewPermissions are those it asks for that what runs was not approved for: all of
them for a plugin new here (D318).

warning.description: Warning is for the admin who approves it, when no key they trust signed it (D280).

code.description: Code is the code to copy (D393); absent for an invite made before codes were kept.

email.description: Email is the address it was mailed to, which alone signs up with it, once (D181).

maxUses.description: MaxUses is how many sign-ups it admits (D371); Used, how many it did.

sent.description:
Sent says the mail went, in the response that mails it; when it did not, the
code can still be copied.

signups.description: Signups are who signed up with it, oldest first.

status.description: Status is whether it admits sign-ups now, by the server's clock, and why not.

problem.description:
Problem says what keeps the code from making an invite: its form, or another
invite having it; absent when it can.

email.description:
Email is the address the invite is for, when it was mailed: the sign-up form fills
it in (D181).

code.description: Code is the one in the invite link.

byEmail.description: ByEmail says invites can be mailed now: switched on, and mail set up (D180).

userId.description: UserID and Email are the account's, absent once it is gone.

name.description: Name is empty for a list's elements.

inviteId.description: InviteID is the invite an approval mailed.

note.description: Note is the requester's, plain text.

status.description: Status is pending until an admin approves or denies it.

pending.description: Pending is how many wait for an admin, for the Invites tab's count.

cancelled.description:
Cancelled are the resting live orders it cancelled as it went on; Left those still
resting, Polymarket not cancelling them.

stored.description: what its nodes stored in workflows

change.description: Change is saving a new graph for a workflow that trades live and is on.

config.description:
And on the instance (D411): changing Config, restarting the server, approving a
plugin version, and every other change to plugins.

goLive.description: GoLive is setting a workflow to trade live, or changing its live wallet.

inAgent.description:
InAgent has them also asked in the agent's own window, where its client can ask
(D409): off to start with.

killOff.description: KillOff is turning the kill switch off.

role.description:
An admin's agents' work on other users (D410): making one an admin or no longer,
disabling or enabling one, raising their caps, letting them write code.

run.description: Run is switching on, or running by hand, a workflow that trades live.

by.description: By is the agent or token behind its run when it was placed (D408); absent for you.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is when a GTD's rest is cancelled.

price.description: Price is the limit: the most a buy pays per share, the least a sell takes.

question.description: Question and Outcome name its market and outcome, when known.

shares.description: Shares asked for, or for a buy of dollars, Dollars.

status.description:
Status open is an order resting on the book, filled in part or not yet, then
filled, canceled or expired with what it filled; pending, a live order sent whose
outcome is not known yet, followed; failed, one that matched but whose trades
failed on chain, undone.

trader.description:
Trader is the wallet whose trade it copies, with their label then; absent for an
order copied from no one.

type.description: SETTLE: a holding closed by its market's resolution

workflowId.description:
WorkflowID is the workflow it came from, and Workflow its name, or the one it had
when it was deleted, Deleted then.

stars.description:
Stars is how many stars GitHub counts for it, while GitHub says and the lookup is
on (D372).

id.description: ID is what the provider calls it, the name an agent node asks for.

name.description: Name is for people: the ID when the provider gives none.

notes.description: Notes explain the node to whoever reads the workflow; they never affect execution.

position.description: Position is where the editor draws the node; it never affects execution.

count.description: Count is how many keys the node remembers now, like the items Only new has seen.

samples.description:
Samples are the first items of each output port. Only runs started by hand keep
them, and execution lists leave them out.

code.description:
Code says it runs code its owner wrote: only users who may write code (the
mayWriteCode of /me) can save it.

items.description: Items describes what the node emits; absent when nobody knows.

outputsParam.description:
OutputsParam names a list param whose values are more output ports, after outputs;
with outputsColumn, a table, that text column of each row naming a port.

plugin.description:
Plugin is the ID of the plugin it comes from, pluginName its name; absent for a
built-in. Trades says it places orders (D309).

remembers.description:
Remembers says it keeps what it saw across runs; /workflows/{id}/nodes/{node}/memory
says how much, and forgets it.

seesItems.description:
SeesItems says its settings' expressions see items, every item it receives on
main, beside each one's fields; a field named items is then item.items.

email.description: Email is by mail, to your account's address, while MailOn (D170).

enabled.description: Enabled is on Telegram, to your linked chat.

group.description:
Group is what the kind is about, to show the kinds under: Workflows, Wallets, Live
orders, Paper orders.

mailOn.description:
MailOn says notifications can go by mail now: an admin allows it, and mail is set up
(D184).

published.description:
Published says it describes itself in a metadata document at its ID: whoever
controls that address wrote it, name and all, which is not the same as being who it
says (A2). A registered client's name is its own word.

site.description:
Site is the host it is from, as ASCII so a lookalike shows as one: its document's,
or its homepage's, unchecked.

allowed.description:
Allowed says the user's grant covers what the client asks: the page approves with
Granted, not asking again. Again says it covers it, but the client comes back
elsewhere than its own site: the page asks for a click, the grant's scopes ticked (A15).

problem.description: Problem is set instead when the request is wrong.

redirectAway.description:
RedirectAway says it goes to another host than the published client's own, and not
this machine: one to warn of (A2).

redirectHost.description: RedirectHost is where the browser goes once the user decides, as ASCII.

redirect.description: Redirect is where to send the browser.

takingTasks.description:
TakingTasks says the agent waits for the tasks of your Local agent nodes now, or did
a moment ago (D413).

askFirst.description:
AskFirst says the page shows it, and where it goes, with a link, rather than sending
the browser there at once: the user never allowed the client (A14).

redirect.description:
Redirect is where to send the browser with it, back to the client; absent, the page
shows it, as the client or its redirect is wrong.

by.description: By is the agent or token behind its run when it was placed (D408); absent for you.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is when a GTD's rest is cancelled.

price.description: Price is the limit: the most a buy pays per share, the least a sell takes.

shares.description: Shares asked for, or for a buy of dollars, Dollars.

status.description:
Status open is an order resting on the book, filled in part or not yet, then
filled, canceled or expired with what it filled; pending, a live order sent whose
outcome is not known yet, followed; failed, one that matched but whose trades
failed on chain, undone.

trader.description:
Trader is the wallet whose trade it copies, with their label then; absent for an
order copied from no one.

type.description: SETTLE: a holding closed by its market's resolution

id.description: ID is the agent's grant, or the token: the log's by takes kind:id.

fee.description: in dollars, on top of a buy, out of a sell

status.description: Status is how far a live fill's trade has come on chain; absent on paper.

open.description:
Open is false until the workflow's first paper order; the rest is then what an
account would start with.

resetAt.description: ResetAt is when it was last started over: orders before it are history.

columns.description:
Columns are the cells of each row of a table, in order, keyed by name: text, a
whole number, a decimal, true or false, or an address, text with options being one
of a few choices. Only the whole table takes an expression.

credentialTypes.description:
CredentialTypes are the kinds of credential a credential param takes: one of the
user's of any of them.

field.description:
Field marks a string, or each element of a list, as a path to a field of the items
the node receives, like spread or outcomes.0.price. FieldKinds, when present, are
the kinds that field may be.

input.description: Input, for a field, is the input port whose items it names; absent for main.

modelsOf.description:
ModelsOf, on text, names the credential param whose key's models it suggests:
/credentials/{id}/models lists them. Any other name can still be typed.

multiline.description: Multiline text is several lines, a prompt, say.

options.description: Options are the allowed values of a string, or of each element of a list.

sensitive.description: Sensitive values, like a webhook URL, are personal: sharing leaves them out.

ids.description: IDs are every pinned workflow of yours, in the order to show them.

data.description:
Data is what its data takes; one no version of which was approved yet has what its
ID left behind as it was uninstalled (D366).

everyone.description: false: only users may use it (D282)

restart.description: Restart says what runs is not what admins decided: a restart applies it (D317).

status.description: Status is how it runs, as it was loaded at start; absent when it was not.

version.description: Version is the approved one, which runs when enabled; empty until the first approval.

by.description: the admin's ID; empty for the server's own doing

stored.description: what its nodes stored in workflows

unsandboxed.description:
Unsandboxed says admins let plugins start without it where it is not: the Config
page's setting.

why.description: why not, when it is not

secret.description: Secret values are write-only: value is null and isSet says whether one is saved.

value.description: Value and Default are typed by kind, as a Setting's are; both null for a secret.

sandboxed.description:
Sandboxed says its process runs under the sandbox. Memory and data are what it took
when last measured, in bytes, memory 0 where it is not watched; the caps are those
it is held to, in bytes.

users.description: who may use it when not everyone

installedBy.description: empty once the account is gone

manifest.description:
Manifest is the version's manifest.json: its nodes, triggers, credential types,
scenarios and settings.

signer.description:
Signer is the trusted key's name that signed it; empty when none an admin trusts
did, keyId saying which key did, if any.

found.description: Found are versions on disk no admin installed, to adopt (D321).

line.description: Line and Column are where in the code a problem is, from 1, columns in characters.

inviteCode.description: InviteCode is required when registration is by invite.

mustVerify.description: MustVerify says the account signs in only once it has opened the link mailed to it.

sent.description: Sent says the link was mailed; when it was not, it can be sent again.

url.description: URL is its page on GitHub, with what changed.

version.description: Version is as it was tagged, without the v, such as 0.1.2.

note.description: Note says who they are and why they would like in: at most 500 characters.

token.description: Token is the one in the mailed link.

problem.description: Problem says why it was not revoked.

revoked.description: Revoked says the Relayer took the revocation; the key is removed here either way.

trigger.description: Trigger is the trigger node to start from; left out means the manual trigger.

day.description: Day and Week are the runs started in the last day and the last week, by hand too.

last.description: Last is the latest run; absent when none is kept.

commit.description: Commit is the full hash it was built from; empty where unknown.

go.description: the Go toolchain it was built with

modified.description: Modified says the checkout had changes not committed.

version.description:
Version is as its release was tagged, such as 0.1.2; dev for a build no release
stamped.

owner.description: Owner is the account that controls the Deposit Wallet, and signs for it.

state.description:
State: signing waits for the owner's signature, authorizing for the chain; the
wallet trades with an active key; a failed one says why in error.

typedData.description:
TypedData is what the owner's browser wallet signs, with eth_signTypedData_v4 on
Polygon.

active.description: Active is the key the wallet trades with.

pending.description:
Pending is the key being authorised, which replaces the active one once confirmed;
or the last that failed.

signatureType.description: SignatureType: 0 EOA, 1 Polymarket proxy, 2 Gnosis Safe, 3 deposit wallet.

signer.description: Signer defaults to the wallet address.

enabled.description: Enabled switches it on Telegram, Email by mail; at least one is given.

apply.description: Apply says when a change takes effect: at once, or after a restart.

pending.description: Pending is set on a changed setting that waits for a restart.

secret.description: Secret values are write-only: value is null and isSet says whether one is saved.

source.description:
Source is where the value comes from. One set by the environment variable Env, or in
the config file under Key, cannot be changed here.

value.description:
Value and Default are typed by kind: text, a whole number, true or false, a
duration as text like "168h", or a list of text. Both are null for a secret.

actorEmail.description: ActorEmail is absent once the account that made the change is gone.

oldValue.description: The values that applied before and after; null for a secret.

nextCursor.description: NextCursor is absent on the last page.

restartPending.description: RestartPending is set when a saved change waits for a restart.

shortcuts.description:
Shortcuts are the keys you set, by action, such as {"undo": "mod+z"}, in place of all
you set before; empty puts every one back to its keys to start with.

signature.description: Signature is what eth_signTypedData_v4 gave, hex.

owner.description: Owner is the browser wallet's account, which must control the wallet.
Owner is the browser wallet's account, which must control the Deposit Wallet.

workflows.description: that have traded in the mode

username.description: Username is the Telegram user's, without the @; not everyone has one.

url.description: URL opens the bot in Telegram; it links whoever opens it, once.

available.description: Available is set while the instance's bot runs, so accounts can link.

problem.description: Problem says why the bot does not run, or what last went wrong. Admins only.

builtIn.description: BuiltIn scenarios ship with Polythought; the others are members' shared workflows.

customNodes.description:
CustomNodes are the custom nodes it brings, code included, as their author had them
when sharing: using it copies them. With one template, not with the list.

mine.description: Mine is set on the workflows you shared.

nodeTypes.description: the kinds of node it uses, without repeats

nodes.description: Nodes and connections come with one template, not with the list.

name.description:
Name makes its type, custom.<name>: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting
with a letter, up to 40. It cannot change.

nodeType.description: NodeType describes it as the node list describes types, for drawing the template.

outputs.description: Outputs are its output ports, in order; it has one input, main.

source.description:
Source is TypeScript exporting run(items, ctx), which gets every item at once and
returns the items, or with several outputs, { port: items }.

type.description: Type is what the template's nodes name it by: custom.<name>.

nextCursor.description: NextCursor is absent on the last page.

to.description: To is the address the test email goes to.

trader.description: Trader is the wallet copied; absent for the orders copied from no one.

workflows.description: that copy them in the mode

closed.description: holdings sold out of, or settled

trader.description: Trader is absent for the orders copied from no one.

closed.description: holdings sold out of, or settled

mode.description: Mode is the one it trades in now, which these are about.

profit.description:
Profit is as its trading page has it: on paper its worth less what it started
with, live what its holdings made, Realized of those sold and Unrealized of those
held, at their marks. Dollars.

unpriced.description: Unpriced are those of them at their cost: no price is known for them now.

volume.description: the dollars its filled orders traded

holdsLive.description:
HoldsLive says it holds live shares: its wallet changes once they are sold or
settled (D202).

liveAvailable.description: LiveAvailable says whether the server places live orders now; Why, why not.

resting.description:
Resting is how many of its live orders rest on the book: switching it off asks
whether to cancel them; going back to paper cancels them.

wallet.description: Wallet is the one live orders spend; absent when none is chosen, or it is gone.

confirm.description:
Confirm is the owner's yes to orders spending real money (D201): going live, or
live from another wallet, needs it.

values.description:
Values to change, by field name. A value left out keeps what is saved, and so does
an empty secret.

confirm.description:
Confirm makes a change that breaks workflows using the node, which is otherwise
refused with breaks_workflows saying which.

name.description:
Name makes its type, custom.<name>: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting
with a letter, up to 40. It cannot change.

outputs.description: Outputs are its output ports, in order; it has one input, main.

source.description:
Source is TypeScript exporting run(items, ctx), which gets every item at once and
returns the items, or with several outputs, { port: items }.

version.description: Version is the version the edit started from; a newer one on the server is a conflict.

values.description:
New values by setting key, typed as PluginSetting.value. null resets a setting to
its default, as does an empty string for a secret.

New values by setting key, typed as Setting.value. null resets a setting to its
default, as does an empty string for a secret.

agentCaps.description:
AgentCaps replace the user's caps on their agents' spend; a cap left out is the
instance's again.

emailVerified.description: EmailVerified true marks the address verified; it cannot be made false.

liveCaps.description: LiveCaps replace the user's caps; a cap left out is the instance's again.

description.description: Description is what it does, up to 1,000 characters; left out keeps the one it has.

version.description: Version is the version the edit started from; a newer one on the server is a conflict.

error.description: Error says why the update failed; Log is the end of what it did.

version.description: the release it updates or updated to

current.description: Current is the server's version, such as 0.1.2, or dev.

error.description: Error says why the last check failed, when it did.

latest.description:
Latest is the newest release GitHub last gave; Newer says it is newer than the
server's, never so for a development build.

on.description: On says the update check is on; off, the server asks GitHub nothing.

updater.description:
Updater says an updater is set up, which Update now asks. Update is its latest
update, absent where it did not answer, and UpdaterError why.

name.description: Name of the new workflow; left out, it takes the template's.

values.description: Values for the template's inputs, by node ID and then param name.

agentCaps.description:
AgentCaps are an admin's caps on their agents' spend a month; those left out are
the instance's (D271).

agentsSeePersonal.description:
AgentsSeePersonal is their choice that agents and API tokens see their workflows'
personal settings (D401, D402); AgentsMayDelete and AgentsMayShare, that they may
delete workflows, custom nodes and credentials and share workflows to the library
(D403, D404); AgentsMayUseCredentials, that they may use credentials in workflows
(D404); AgentsMayAnswer, that they may answer their workflows' questions (D405).

codeChosen.description:
CodeChosen says an admin picked them to write code, which counts while code access
is "chosen".

dashboard.description: Dashboard is how you set the workflows' dashboard (D429): yours, in /me only.

killStopsAgents.description: KillStopsAgents is their choice that their kill switch stops their agents too.

liveCaps.description: LiveCaps are an admin's caps for them; those left out are the instance's (D222).

liveConfirm.description: LiveConfirm is which of their tokens' and agents' live actions wait for them (D406).

liveStopped.description:
LiveStopped says their kill switch is on, since LiveStoppedAt: their workflows place
no live orders (D220).

mayWriteCode.description:
MayWriteCode says whether they may write code now, as code access and CodeChosen
have it.

shortcuts.description:
Shortcuts are the keys you set for the workflow editor's shortcuts, by action (D420):
yours, in /me only.

nextCursor.description: NextCursor is absent on the last page.

email.description: Email is the account's address, now verified, for the sign-in form.

token.description: Token is the one in the mailed link.

hasKey.description: HasKey says it has a key to trade with: its private key, or a session key.

hasSessionKey.description: HasSessionKey says the key is an authorised session key.

heartbeat.description: Heartbeat says Polymarket cancels its resting orders when the server goes quiet.

cash.description: Cash is the wallet's pUSD on Polymarket's CLOB, what its live orders spend.

takesKeys.description: TakesKeys says whether the instance takes private keys now, as an admin set it.

takesSessionKeys.description:
TakesSessionKeys says whether it offers session keys: once an admin has entered a
Builder key.

actedBy.description:
ActedBy is the agent or token that switched it on, or changed it while on, named on
its runs until it is switched again (D407); absent for you.

description.description: Description is what it does, in your words; searched with its name.

pin.description: Pin is its place among your pinned workflows, from 1; absent when it is not pinned.

workflow.description:
Workflow is what the code builds. Code says nothing of positions: every node's is
0, 0, for the editor to place.

source.description:
Source is TypeScript whose default export is a workflow made with
@polythought/workflow.

description.description: Description is what it does, up to 1,000 characters; left out keeps the one it has.

nextCursor.description: NextCursor is absent on the last page.

problems.description: Problems are what saving the workflow as it is would refuse; empty when none.

trading.description: Trading is what it made in the mode it trades in now; absent until it has traded in it.

day.description: Day and Week are all their runs, started in the last day and the last week.

paper.description: Paper and Live add up the workflows trading in each mode, never one into the other.

traders.description:
Traders are what copying each trader came to across the workflows, in each mode,
the most profitable first, copied from no one last.

APIToken.description: Personal API token: Authorization: Bearer pt_...

SessionCookie.description: Browser session cookie, set by POST /auth/login; __Host-polythought_session when the app is served over https.
SessionCookie.name: polythought_session
